- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecast tends to be too low in the early part of the 30-day window, then gradually increases — suggesting a lag in capturing recent price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.80 → 80.24), model overreacts and overshoots, then corrects too slowly.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after peaks.
- Forecast often misses the true mean of recent 30-day history, especially in the middle-to-late period.
- Model exhibits bias toward lower values in the first 5–7 days, then gradually adjusts — suggesting a delayed calibration to recent trends.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are systematically too low in the first 10 days, then converge toward true values — indicating a lag in capturing short-term volatility.
